title: Inside Nepal’s security response after Sunsari violence - The Kathmandu Post
description: Inside Nepal’s security response after Sunsari violence  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
A day after communal violence in Sunsari’s Dewanganj Rural Municipality left one person dead and 22 others injured, Nepal’s top security officials gathered at the government’s central secretariat to assess the situation, discuss the risk of further escalation, and decide how the state should respond. The Central Security Committee meeting, held at 5 pm on July 27 under the chairmanship of Home Minister Sudan Gurung, brought together senior officials from Nepal’s security and administrative establishment: Nepali Army Lieutenant General Pradeep KC, Home Ministry Secretary Raj Kumar Shrestha, Defence Ministry Secretary Kedarnath Sharma, Nepal Police Inspector General Dan Bahadur Karki, Armed Police Force Inspector General Narayan Dutta Poudel, and National Investigation Department Chief Tekendra Karki. The meeting at the Home Ministry continued until around 9 pm. The discussion was held after authorities faced questions over the handling of the Dewanganj incident. Earlier that day, the government had begun changing key security officials responsible for the area. Koshi Province Police Chief Binod Ghimire was recalled and was replaced by DIG Shekhar Khanal from Nepal Police Headquarters. Sunsari Chief District Officer Basudev Ghimire was transferred and replaced by Sankhuwasabha CDO Ishwari Prasad Aryal. Sunsari Police Chief SP Keshav Thebe was recalled, and SP Pushparaj Malla from Gautam Buddha International Airport was sent to Sunsari.

Arjun Subedi/TKP

The DSP of the Armed Police Force company based in Kaptanganj, Nandakishor Mahato, who was present in the area during the incident, was also recalled and replaced by DSP Madan Nath from Armed Police Force Headquarters. At least five people — including security officials and ministry officials familiar with the meeting — told Kantipur what transpired during the July 27 discussion. According to one official, who spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter, Home Minister Gurung appeared visibly upset with the security response. Gurung, the official said, also raised concerns over increasing smuggling activities along the border, the lack of effective action against smuggling, and what he described as mistakes by security agencies during the communal violence in Sunsari. Gurung directed authorities to increase security deployment along the border and install drones and CCTV cameras. The official said the discussion appeared to be moving away from the immediate crisis and measures to address it. “He was fidgety, at times extremely dissatisfied that security personnel had failed to do their work,” the official added. Meanwhile, concerns were mounting over whether tensions could escalate further. During the Central Security Committee meeting, security chiefs raised the possibility that the violence could spread to other parts of the country. According to officials present at the meeting, Army Lieutenant General Pradeep KC and the chiefs of Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, and the National Investigation Department — Dan Bahadur Karki, Narayan Dutta Poudel, and Tekendra Karki — emphasised the need for measures to manage the situation and prevent similar incidents elsewhere. Another account of the meeting, from a source familiar with the discussion, described a different emphasis from the military side. Army Lt. General KC, according to the security source, argued that field-level security agencies and officials were already aware of the operational requirements and that the role of the centre should be “to coordinate rather than direct every tactical decision.” The source said Lt. General KC explained that decisions such as where to deploy security personnel, where to position equipment such as CCTV cameras and drones, and how to mobilise forces were matters traditionally handled at the field level. “These are tactical and strategic issues,” the source quoted Lt. General KC as saying. “Such matters have been handled from the field rather than from above, and security personnel should be deployed effectively according to that approach.” KC told the meeting that field-level mechanisms were aware of the situation and that coordination from the centre was necessary. The source said the heads of other security agencies also informed the meeting that efforts were underway to bring the situation under control. However, the source claimed that the Home Minister appeared more focused on expressing anger than listening to those assessments. “At such a time, such a temperament does not help,” the source added. On July 28, Home Minister Gurung held another security meeting at the Home Ministry with officials from Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, and the National Investigation Department. The meeting instructed subordinate agencies to work toward maintaining social harmony. However, tensions continued, and violent demonstrations between the two groups resumed in the evening. The incident also triggered a political response. On July 29, an all-party meeting was held on the initiative of Rabi Lamichhane, chairman of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party. The meeting included representatives of parties represented in Parliament — RSP, Nepali Congress, UML, Nepali Communist Party, Shram Sanskriti Party and Rastriya Prajatantra Party — as well as leaders of parties outside Parliament, including Janata Samajbadi Party, Janamat Party, and JSP Nepal. Prime Minister Balendra Shah did not attend the meeting. Nor did Home Minister Gurung. The meeting issued a seven-point agreement, including condolences for those killed in the incident, sympathy for the victims and the injured, an appeal for social harmony and peace, calls for local-level all-party mechanisms, stronger coordination and leadership from the centre, control of rumours, and the responsible use of social media.

Arjun Subedi/TKP

Questions over Nepal’s security response model The Sunsari incident has once again raised broader questions about how Nepal manages communal tensions and coordinates security responses across its federal structure. Under Nepal’s federal system, provincial police chiefs legally come under the authority of provincial governments. Provincial security committees, led by provincial home ministers, are also responsible for security management and developing strategies. However, a security official said the transfer of the Koshi Province police chief was carried out without coordination with the provincial government. “This reflects a wider problem in Nepal’s transition to federal governance,” the official added. The District Administration Office (headed by the Chief District Officer) remains under the direct command and control of the federal government. Since laws related to the Nepal Police and the federal civil service have not been fully implemented, transfers and deployments of Chief District Officers and provincial police structures continue to be controlled from Kathmandu, the federal capital. As a result, when security incidents occur in the provinces, coordination between Chief District Officers and provincial mechanisms has not yet become an established practice. Since Chief District Officers, who lead the district security committees, are direct appointees of the Home Ministry, when security incidents occur, they report to Kathmandu, not to the provincial minister for internal affairs, who heads the provincial security committee. This has created a gap between federal institutions and provincial structures, according to officials familiar with the issue. Incidents affecting religious and communal harmony have occurred in different parts of the country in the past as well. However, security forces are often deployed only after tensions have already escalated. Critics argue that the current approach focuses heavily on a control mechanism — using security forces to contain situations after they become violent. A different approach would focus on management and prevention, involving local governments, provincial governments, federal agencies, civil society groups, and representatives of different communities before tensions turn into violence. Such an approach would require dialogue and coordination mechanisms to identify warning signs and prevent escalation. The argument is that managing communal tensions cannot rely only on force after violence occurs; it requires sustained engagement before a crisis develops. Pradhumna Karki, a former AIG of Nepal Police, said the situation in Devanganj, Sunsari, along with similar incidents that have occurred in different places at different times, suggests that weaknesses in crowd control and crowd management have often resulted in the loss of life and property and disrupted social harmony. “Different religious communities have their own ways of life, customs and beliefs. They coexist by maintaining social and religious harmony,” he told Kantipur. “However, there are always elements that seek to provoke tensions between them. This is where the security apparatus and the administration must focus their attention.” Karki also pointed to the lack of crowd-control capacity and non-lethal equipment within the security agencies. “There is a tendency to acknowledge these shortages only after an incident has occurred — saying that this or that resource was lacking and promising that such shortages will not be allowed in the future,” he said. “This approach needs to end. The necessary resources should be made available in time.” A prior risk assessment is key, he said, as it helps avert a crisis. “Had the administration, local government, civil society, political parties and other stakeholders assessed the sensitivity of the issue in advance and acted accordingly, the situation would not have deteriorated.” Questions over intelligence assessment The role of Nepal’s National Investigation Department has also come under scrutiny following the Sunsari incident. The National Investigation Department, which was recently brought under the Prime Minister’s Office, is the country’s main intelligence agency. It is mandated to collect information independently and assess situations, with reports expected to move through a chain of command before other security agencies develop strategies based on those assessments. Questions have been raised about whether the department had adequately assessed the situation before the Sunsari violence. The National Investigation Department’s Koshi Province chief is Investigation Director Indra Lama, a DIG-level officer. Its Sunsari chief is Deputy Investigation Director Bimal Ghimire, an SP-level officer. While officials from other security agencies and the Chief District Officer were recalled or transferred after the incident, officials from the National Investigation Department continued in their positions. Devraj Bhatta, a former Additional Chief Investigation Director at the National Investigation Department, said there were indications that warning signs had emerged well before the Sunsari incident but were ignored. “While the local government, security agencies and the administration overlooked those warning signs, the intelligence agencies assigned to monitor the situation also do not appear to have carried out their primary responsibilities,” Bhatta told Kantipur. “Another question is this: if similar incidents had occurred in the past, why were precautionary measures and a strategy not put in place beforehand? That is the central question.” Bhatta also believes that, after the incident occurred, intervention from the centre to prevent further escalation and restore calm either came too late or was neglected. “All of these factors contributed to the unfortunate incident in Sunsari, which disrupted religious and social harmony,” he said. “The police, Armed Police Force, intelligence agencies and the local administration were preoccupied with their own interests. Instead of assessing the situation properly, they were focused on their own priorities.”

घटना के दौरान इलाका मे मौजूद कप्तानगंज स्थित सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल कंपनी के डीएसपी नंदकिशोर महतो के सेहो वापस बजा क ओकर जगह पर सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल मुख्यालय स डीएसपी मदन नाथ के राखल गेल। कम स॑ कम पांच लोगऽ न॑ – जेकरा म॑ सुरक्षा अधिकारी आरू बैठक स॑ परिचित मंत्रालय केरऽ अधिकारी भी शामिल छै – न॑ कान्तिपुर क॑ बतैलकै कि २७ जुलाई केरऽ चर्चा के दौरान जे कुछ घटलै । मामला के संवेदनशीलता के कारण नाम नै बताबै के शर्त पर बात करै वाला एक अधिकारी के अनुसार सुरक्षा प्रतिक्रिया स॑ गृहमंत्री गुरुंग दृष्टिगोचर रूप स॑ परेशान नजर ऐलै । अधिकारी नँ कहलकै कि गुरुंग नँ सीमा के साथ बढ़तौ तस्करी गतिविधि, तस्करी के खिलाफ प्रभावी कार्रवाई के कमी आरू सुनसरी मँ सांप्रदायिक हिंसा के दौरान सुरक्षा एजेंसी सिनी द्वारा गलती के रूप मँ भी चिंता व्यक्त करलकै । गुरुंग नँ अधिकारियौ क सीमा के साथ सुरक्षा तैनाती बढ़ाबै आरू ड्रोन आरू सीसीटीवी कैमरा लगाबै के निर्देश देलकै । अधिकारी कहला जे चर्चा तत्काल संकट आ ओकरा दूर करबाक उपाय स दूर भ रहल देखा रहल अछि। अधिकारी आगू कहलनि जे, ओ चंचल छलाह, कखनो काल एहि बात सं अत्यंत असंतुष्ट छलाह जे सुरक्षाकर्मी अपन काज नहि क सकलाह। एम्हर एहि बात पर चिंता बढ़ि रहल छल जे तनाव आओर बढ़ि सकैत अछि कि नहि. केन्द्रीय सुरक्षा समिति के बैसार के दौरान सुरक्षा प्रमुख सब ई संभावना उठैलकै कि ई हिंसा देश के दोसरऽ भाग म॑ भी फैल॑ सकै छै । बैसारमे उपस्थित अधिकारीसबके अनुसार सेना लेफ्टिनेंट जनरल प्रदीप केसी आ नेपाल प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल, आ राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभागके प्रमुख — दानबहादुर कार्की, नारायण दत्ता पौडेल, आ टेकेन्द्र कार्की — परिस्थितिके व्यवस्थापन आ अन्यत्र एहने घटनाके रोकथामके उपायके आवश्यकतामे जोर देलक । बैठक केरऽ एगो आरू विवरण, जेकरा म॑ चर्चा स॑ परिचित स्रोत स॑ मिललऽ छै, म॑ सैन्य पक्ष स॑ अलग जोर के वर्णन करलऽ गेलऽ छै । सुरक्षा सूत्र के अनुसार सेना के लेफ्टिनेंट जनरल केसी के तर्क छेलै कि फील्ड स्तर के सुरक्षा एजेंसी आरू अधिकारी सिनी क॑ परिचालन संबंधी आवश्यकता के बारे म॑ पहल॑ स॑ ही पता छै आरू केंद्र के भूमिका “हर सामरिक फैसला क॑ निर्देशित करै के बजाय समन्वय करना” होना चाहियऽ । सूत्र नँ कहलकै कि लेफ्टिनेंट जनरल केसी नँ बतैलकै कि सुरक्षा कर्मी क कहाँ तैनात करलौ जाय, सीसीटीवी कैमरा आरू ड्रोन जैसनौ उपकरण क कहाँ रखलौ जैतै, आरू बल क कोना जुटाबै के छै, ई तरह के फैसला परंपरागत रूप स॑ मैदान स्तर प संभाललौ जाय वाला मामला छेलै । सूत्र लेफ्टिनेंट जनरल केसी के हवाला स कहलनि जे, ई सामरिक आ रणनीतिक मुद्दा अछि। “एहन मामला ऊपर स नहि बल्कि मैदान स निपटल गेल अछि, आ सुरक्षा कर्मी कए ओहि दृष्टिकोण क अनुसार प्रभावी ढंग स तैनात करबाक चाही।” केसी बैसार मे कहला जे फील्ड लेवल क तंत्र कए एहि स्थिति क जानकारी अछि आ केंद्र स समन्वय जरूरी अछि। सूत्र कहलनि जे, अन्य सुरक्षा एजेंसी के प्रमुख सेहो बैसार के जानकारी देलखिन्ह जे स्थिति के काबू मे अनबाक प्रयास चलि रहल अछि। हालांकि सूत्र क दावा अछि जे गृहमंत्री ओहि आकलन कए सुनबा स बेसी आक्रोश व्यक्त करबा पर केंद्रित देखा रहल छथि। सूत्र आगू कहलनि जे, एहन समय मे एहन स्वभाव कोनो मदद नहि करैत अछि। २८ जुलैके गृहमन्त्री गुरुङ नेपाल प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल, आ राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभागके अधिकारीसबके साथ गृहमन्त्रालयमे दोसर सुरक्षा बैसार करल छल । बैसार मे अधीनस्थ एजेंसी कए सामाजिक सौहार्द कायम रखबाक दिशा मे काज करबाक निर्देश देल गेल। मुदा, तनाव जारी रहल, आ साँझ मे दुनू समूहक बीच हिंसक प्रदर्शन फेर सं शुरू भ गेल. एहि घटना स राजनीतिक प्रतिक्रिया सेहो शुरू भ गेल। 29 जुलाई कए सत्तारूढ़ राष्ट्रिय स्वतंत्र पार्टी क अध्यक्ष रबी लामिछाने क पहल पर सर्वदलीय बैसार भेल छल । बैसार मे संसद मे प्रतिनिधित्व करय वाला दल के प्रतिनिधि — आरएसपी, नेपाली कांग्रेस, एमाले, नेपाली कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी, श्रम संस्कृति पार्टी आ राष्ट्रीय प्रजातंत्र पार्टी के प्रतिनिधि के संग संग संसद सं बाहर के दल के नेता, जाहि मे जनता समाजबादी पार्टी, जनमत पार्टी, आ जसपा नेपाल शामिल छल. प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह बैसारमे उपस्थित नहि भेलाह । आ ने गृहमंत्री गुरुंग। बैठक म॑ सात सूत्री समझौता जारी करलऽ गेलै, जेकरा म॑ ई घटना म॑ मारलऽ गेलऽ लोगऽ के प्रति शोक संवेदना, पीड़ित आरू घायलऽ के प्रति सहानुभूति, सामाजिक सौहार्द आरू शांति के अपील, स्थानीय स्तर के सर्वदलीय तंत्र, केंद्र स॑ मजबूत समन्वय आरू नेतृत्व, अफवाहऽ प॑ नियंत्रण, आरू सोशल मीडिया के जिम्मेदार उपयोग के आह्वान शामिल छै ।

अर्जुन सुबेदी/टीकेपी

नेपाल केरऽ सुरक्षा प्रतिक्रिया मॉडल प॑ सवाल सुनसरी केरऽ घटना न॑ एक बार फेरू ई बात प॑ व्यापक सवाल उठैलकै कि नेपाल अपनऽ संघीय संरचना भर म॑ साम्प्रदायिक तनाव क॑ कोना प्रबंधित करै छै आरू सुरक्षा प्रतिक्रिया के समन्वय करै छै । नेपाल के संघीय व्यवस्था के तहत प्रांतीय पुलिस प्रमुख कानूनी तौर पर प्रांतीय सरकार के अधिकार में आबै छै. प्रांतीय गृहमंत्री के नेतृत्व में प्रांतीय सुरक्षा समिति के जिम्मेदारी सुरक्षा प्रबंधन आरू रणनीति बनाबै के भी छै । मुदा एकटा सुरक्षा अधिकारी के कहनाय छनि जे कोशी प्रांत के थानाध्यक्ष के तबादला प्रांतीय सरकार के संग बिना समन्वय केने भेल अछि. अधिकारी आगू कहलनि जे, ई नेपाल के संघीय शासन मे संक्रमण मे व्यापक समस्या के दर्शाबैत अछि। जिला प्रशासन कार्यालय (मुख्य जिल्ला अधिकारी के नेतृत्व में) संघीय सरकार के प्रत्यक्ष कमान आ नियंत्रण में रहैत अछि | नेपाल प्रहरी आ संघीय सिविल सेवासँ सम्बन्धित कानून पूर्ण रूपसँ लागू नै भेलाक कारण संघीय राजधानी काठमाण्डौसँ मुख्य जिल्ला अधिकारी आ प्रान्तीय प्रहरी संरचनाके स्थानान्तरण आ तैनाती पर नियंत्रण जारी अछि । एकरऽ परिणाम ई छै कि जब॑ प्रांतऽ म॑ सुरक्षा केरऽ घटना घटै छै त॑ मुख्य जिला अधिकारी आरू प्रांतीय तंत्र के बीच समन्वय अभी तलक स्थापित प्रथा नै बनी गेलऽ छै । जिल्ला सुरक्षा समिति के नेतृत्व करय वाला मुख्य जिल्ला अधिकारी गृह मंत्रालय के सीधा नियुक्ति के कारण सुरक्षा के घटना घटला पर काठमांडू के रिपोर्ट करैत छथि, प्रांतीय आतंरिक मामिला के मंत्री के नहिं, जे प्रांतीय सुरक्षा समिति के प्रमुख छथि. एहि स संघीय संस्था आ प्रांतीय संरचना क बीच अंतर पैदा भ गेल अछि, मुद्दा स परिचित अधिकारी क कहब अछि। धार्मिक आरू साम्प्रदायिक सौहार्द क॑ प्रभावित करै वाला घटना पूर्व म॑ भी देश केरऽ विभिन्न भागऽ म॑ घटित होय चुकलऽ छै । लेकिन सुरक्षा बल केरऽ तैनाती अक्सर तनाव पहलें स॑ बढ़ला के बाद ही करलऽ जाय छै । आलोचकऽ के तर्क छै कि वर्तमान दृष्टिकोण एगो नियंत्रण तंत्र प॑ बहुत केंद्रित छै — सुरक्षा बलऽ के उपयोग करी क॑ हिंसक होय के बाद परिस्थिति क॑ रोकै लेली । एकटा अलग दृष्टिकोण प्रबंधन आ रोकथाम पर केंद्रित होयत, जाहि मे स्थानीय सरकार, प्रांतीय सरकार, संघीय एजेंसी, नागरिक समाज समूह, आ विभिन्न समुदायक कें प्रतिनिधि शामिल होयत, तखन तनाव हिंसा मे बदलल जायत. ऐन्हऽ दृष्टिकोण लेली चेतावनी संकेतऽ के पहचान करै आरू बढ़ोत्तरी क॑ रोकै लेली संवाद आरू समन्वय तंत्र के जरूरत होतै । तर्क ई छै कि साम्प्रदायिक तनाव के प्रबंधन केवल हिंसा के बाद बल पर भरोसा नै करी सकै छै; संकट कें विकास सं पहिले एकरा मे लगातार जुड़ाव कें आवश्यकता होयत छै. नेपाल प्रहरीके पूर्व एआइजी प्रधान कार्की सुनसरीके देवगंजके स्थितिके साथ साथ विभिन्न समयमे विभिन्न अपन जीवन-शैली, रीति-रिवाज आ मान्यता होइत छैक, सामाजिक आ धार्मिक सौहार्द कायम राखि ओकर सह-अस्तित्व होइत छैक। “हालांकि, हमेशा एहन तत्व रहैत अछि जे दुनू के बीच तनाव पैदा करय चाहैत अछि। सुरक्षा तंत्र आ title: Gurugram to Nepal in 1 day? New highway set to redraw NCR’s road-trip map - The Tribune
description: Gurugram to Nepal in 1 day? New highway set to redraw NCR’s road-trip map  The Tribune
publisher.title: The Tribune
full_article:
Gurugram residents planning a Himalayan getaway may soon be able to reach the Nepal border in a single day, with the nearly completed Gorakhpur-Sonauli highway set to cut travel time from the city to around 10 hours, down from the current 17-hour journey. The route runs via Delhi, Ghaziabad and the Purvanchal Expressway to Gorakhpur—a stretch of about 653 km that currently takes around 14 hours and 30 minutes. From there, the route continues via Campierganj, Pharenda and Nautanwa to the Sonauli border crossing, a distance of around 90-95 km that presently takes 2.5 to 3 hours due to congestion on the existing two-lane road. Once the new four-lane corridor becomes operational, the second leg is expected to take just over an hour, reducing the total travel time from Gurugram to Sonauli to around 8.5 to 9 hours for a distance of approximately 745-750 km. Advertisement googletag.cmd.push((function(){googletag.display("div-gpt-ad-1722694474562-0")})) Officials, during a recent project review, said the Gorakhpur-Sonauli four-lane project is progressing rapidly and will strengthen connectivity with the India-Nepal border and the Buddhist tourism circuit, besides boosting trade, tourism and freight movement. The upgraded highway includes a railway bridge, two flyovers, 24 underpasses, more than 100 culverts and nearly 68 km of service roads. The infrastructure is aimed at easing the movement of trucks and pilgrims, which currently face bottlenecks at the Sonauli crossing. The project also aligns with a broader plan to eventually extend the corridor towards Siliguri in West Bengal, creating a larger high-speed link connecting northern and eastern India. The extension could position Gorakhpur as a key transit hub for NCR travellers heading further east as well as into Nepal. For Gurugram’s growing road-trip community, already benefiting from improved connectivity to destinations such as Nainital and Mussoorie, Nepal is set to become another convenient driving destination. While Kathmandu will remain another 9-12 hours beyond the border via Bhairahawa, Butwal and Mugling—as the Nepal-side road is not part of this project—border towns such as Sonauli, Bhairahawa and Lumbini, the birthplace of Lord Buddha, will effectively come within a single day’s drive from the city. Officials have not announced a firm inauguration date, though the project is being monitored for completion by the end of 2026. full_article:
The UN's International Organization for Migration (IOM) says between 100,000 to 300,000 Nepalis move to India each year.

There is no official count of how many people migrate annually, as India and Nepal have shared an open border since 1950.

The UN’s crime agency, the UNODC, estimates that in South Asia alone, human trafficking generates $52 billion in annual profits.
